original.description: Today, mission ground segment systems face increasingly sophisticated and fast-movingcyber threats that can evade static or rule-based detection tools and overwhelm traditionalrecovery procedures. As attacks grow more pervasive, dynamic and subtle, currentapproaches, such as rule-based or ticket driven responses struggle to react at the requiredspeed, resulting in prolonged attacker dwelltime and potential disruption of critical missionoperations, if an attack is detected at all.Real-time automated responses or self-healing' mechanisms, such as fall-back tosecure/minimum configurations, runtime policy/rule change, trusted state reconstitution, orrapid tear-down and re-deploy of compromised systems, can reduce the time required tocontain threats. The aim is to reduce attacker dwell time and maintain service continuityduring otherwise high impact incidents. This activity addresses that gap by developing anddemonstrating a proof-of-concept autonomous self-healing architecture tailored to thecritical mission operations ground segment. It will provide an adaptive resilience mechanismaddressing detection, isolation and recovery with an emphasis on service continuity. Moderntechnologies and techniques are to be explored including:- declarative infrastructure as code for cloud-agnostic redundancy and recovery automation- decoupled micro-service isolation and zero-trust architectures- secure root of trust and immutable system configuration restoration- failure prediction- adaptive response mechanisms leveraging machine learning.The proof-of-concept demonstrator will be integrated into a multi-mission, cloud nativeground segment scenario, leveraging existing (Cyber) Security Operations Centres((C)SOC) monitoring and diagnostic capabilities to ensure operational relevance. It willdemonstrate end to enddetection, isolation, and recovery in the context of missionmonitoring and control systems operating in the loop.

original.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to enhance the existing Open Radio Access Network (ORAN) framework to support 5G/6G Non-Terrestrial-Network (NTN) payloads, while integrating the ORAN adaptations with conventional ground segment control centres.Targeted Improvements:1) Adapt the of Enhanced Open Radio Access Network (ORAN) interfaces to support Non-Terrestrial-Network (NTN) 5G/6G payload2) Improve the ORAN Transport network layer3) Enable the Integration of ORAN interfaces into the ground segment operations for system interoperability4) Enable new applications for NTN payloads.Description: Open Radio Access Network (ORAN) specifications are on the brink of reforming the 3GPP radio network fabric through the development and standardisation of open interfaces that provide vendor interoperability, disaggregation of radio protocol stack, access to Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML enabled Radio Intelligent Controllers (RICs) and a framework for Service Management and Orchestration (SMO). The complexity required for the management and optimisation of hybrid TN/NTN (terrestrial/non-terrestrial network) radio platforms, make ORAN an ideal candidate for handling mobility, resource allocation, quality of Service optimisation, multi-connectivity, and spectrum sharing amongothers.Currently a solid background exists to build upon and expand the current ORAN standards and interfaces to support the NTN regenerative payloads, the interworking between TN/NTN nodes and the open interface integration with ground segment Network Operations Centres (NOCs).To tackle the main challenges, this activity is expected to:1) Enhance ORAN architectures with respect to the deployment of optimised interfaces between ground and space.2) Support the adaptation of the ORAN application protocol and service models, to support the 5G/6G NTN payloads.3) Optimise the ORAN transport network association to support the satellite motion out of aspecific geographical area.4) Develop and test real and non-real time Radio Intelligent Controller (RIC) enabled AI/ML applications (xApps, rApps) for NTN node mobility, traffic steering, quality of serviceoptimisation and resource allocation.5) Integrate the ORAN open interfaces with a real or emulated/simulated NOC terminating the interface, to optimise the resource allocation of regenerative NTN nodes.6) Integrate the TN and NTN existing nodes under the same RIC and Service Management and Orchestration (SMO) platform.7) Deliver an end-to-end testbed that follows the OpenRAN workflow and demonstrate the performances for various scenarios with different service requirements.

original.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop advanced and post-quantum Subscriber Identity Module (SIMs) for 5G/6G NTN. The focus is to improve user anonymity for robust non-terrestrialnetworks (NTNs) used for governmental applications which have a more urgent need for post-quantum anonymity protection than the commercial market. These SIMs shall implementsecurity improvements of the part of the primary authentication protocol which is implemented in the SIM. Additionally, the corresponding SIM provisioning infrastructure and the corenetwork responsible for the communication with the SIMs will be developed.TargetedImprovements: Enablinga European or Canadian source for robust NTN SIM (Physical Universal Integrated Circuit Card (UICC) or Embedded UICC (eUICC)) for 5G/6G satellite constellation withhardened primary authentication protocolDescription: Current 5G Universal Subscriber Identity Modules (USIMs) to be used in Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) for Satellite Communication (SATCOM) terminals lack adequate protectionagainst user tracking when assuming a quantum attacker. While 3GPP is working on the migration to post-quantum cryptography, the privacy needs in governmental NTN networks arehigher than in usual mobile networks and regulatory needs will require the full post-Quantum migration as early as 2030 for governmental communication solutions. An appropriatesolution therefore needs to be developed earlier than the 3GPP timeline foresees.The activity will design, develop and test prototypes of advanced 5G/6G USIMs integrating security improvements to the primary authentication protocol (user tracking enhancements inNTNs and anticipated regulatory requirements for post-quantum cryptography), with all components adhering to GSMA/ETSI security standards and targeting Common Criteria evaluationto prepare for future accreditation.The activity will evaluate two implementation paths to address this need: Physical Universal Integrated Circuit Card (UICC) development, potentially as an applet on an existing smartcard platform, or Embedded UICC (eUICC) with appropriate SIM profiles for multi-provider service access. Post-Quantum Key Exchange Management (KEM) implementations on smartcards prove the technical feasibility of implementing such protocols in the UICC approach.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach.The first phase will study the implementation of post quantum security in the authentication protocol and perform a trade-off analysis between the two implementation paths. It will designand develop an initial prototype of the USIM and provisioning infrastructure compatible with standardised 3GPP interfaces between USIM and Mobile Equipment and perform the designof the security functions of the Core network solution to interoperate with the USIM. Phase 1 deliverables consist of architecture and design documents, initial documents to prepare thecertification, software prototype and adapted core network functions to interoperate with the software. The budget for Phase 1 is up to 700 kEuros.In the second phase, the activity will further develop and test the USIM components (UICC or eUICC), create the complete SIM provisioning infrastructure, and develop and test the corenetwork security functionsincluding the Subscriber Identifier De-concealing Function (SIDF) to support enhanced authentication of the USIM to the network. Phase 2 deliverables includethe adaptation of smart card including applet design and SIM printer or chip development for eUICC and refined certification preparation.During the activity, dissemination towards 3GPP standardisation shall be performed to ensure futureindustry adoption.

original.description: NAVISP-EL1-117-Resilience Techniques and Algorithms for GNSS Space Receivers in Interference, Jamming and Spoofing Conditions: Thisactivity aims to enhance the resilience of GNSS space receivers against interference, jamming, and spoofing in LEO. It will study and evaluate novel detection and mitigation techniques, including potential spin-in from terrestrial applications. The scope includesdefining standardized threats and scenarios to support future specifications for space receivers. The work involves simulations andearly prototyping of selected technologies to validate concepts.
